correctness.rationale: The semisimple annihilating-ideal graph is the strong Boolean disjointness graph on nonempty proper subsets. For any connected graph, a landmark set fails on a pair exactly when it avoids that pair’s distinguishing set, so the threshold is \(|V|-\min|D(u,v)|+1\). Partitioning two supports into intersection, the two one-sided differences, and the outside region yields the four exhaustive formulas in RESULT.md. Minimizing them gives the unique sharp mechanism: a nested pair differing in one coordinate with the lower support and upper complement as balanced as possible. The exceptional ranks \(n=2,3\) are handled directly. An independent breadth-first replay for ranks through 8 reproduced the threshold and the full minimizing-pair classification; the finite replay is corroborative only.

value.rationale: Metric-dimension threshold is a natural robustness invariant for resolving sets, and the strong Boolean graph is a canonical algebraic/combinatorial family.
